notes.meaning: John tells Christians not to believe every person who claims to speak for God. Believers must test teachers against the scriptures, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. Being excited or sincere does not mean a person teaches the truth.

The main test of any religious teacher is what they say about Jesus. A person led by the Spirit of God openly teaches that Jesus Christ is truly God who came to earth in a real human body. This basic truth shows that the teacher is on God's side.

Any teacher who refuses to confess that Jesus came in the flesh does not come from God. This false teaching comes from the spirit of the antichrist, which opposes Christ and tries to replace Him. The disciples had heard this spirit was coming, and it was already at work through deceivers.

John comforts believers by telling them they belong to God's family and have already stood strong against false teachers. They won this victory because the Holy Spirit living in them is far stronger than Satan, who rules the sinful world. Christians can walk in courage instead of fear.

The false teachers belong to the unbelieving world and share its ways of thinking. Because their message pleases human desires and fits the spirit of the age, worldly people gladly listen to them. A large following does not prove that a teacher speaks God's truth.

John and the other apostles were sent by God, so anyone who truly knows God listens to what they teach. People who do not belong to God reject the apostles' message. Comparing what someone teaches with the apostles' words shows whether they have the Holy Spirit of truth or the spirit of lies.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching understands the call to listen to 'us' as pointing to the living authority of the church and its bishops, not only the written words of the first apostles.

notes.meaning: John urges Christians to love one another because all true love comes from God. Anyone who shows real, selfless love has been born into God's family and knows Him well. Spiritual rebirth always changes a person's heart so they begin to care for others.

A person who does not love does not know God at all, because love is God's very nature. Love is not just something God decides to do; it is who He is at His very heart. Anyone whose life is empty of love shows that they have never experienced Him.

God revealed His great love by sending His one and only Son into this world. We were spiritually dead because of sin, but Jesus came so we could receive true and everlasting life. Giving His Son was the greatest proof of love God could ever give.

True love is defined by God's action, not ours. We did not love God first, but He loved us while we were still His enemies. He showed this love by sending His Son as an atoning sacrifice—an offering that pays for our sins and turns away God's anger so we can be forgiven.

Since God loved unworthy sinners with such deep sacrifice, believers have a duty to love each other in the same way. God's mercy gives Christians both the pattern and the reason for caring for their brothers and sisters. We show God's love to others when we treat them kindly.

No human being has ever seen God with physical eyes. Even so, when believers love one another, God makes His home inside them and His love reaches its full purpose in their lives. The unseen God becomes visible to the world through the loving deeds of His people.

Believers can be sure they live in God and He lives in them because He has given them His Holy Spirit. The Spirit gives Christians the inner desire and power to love others and follow Christ. This shared spiritual life is steady proof of true friendship with God.

John and his fellow apostles saw Jesus with their own eyes and testified to what they witnessed. They announced the message that God the Father sent His Son to rescue the world from the penalty of sin. This eyewitness testimony gives all Christians a solid ground for their faith.

Whoever openly states from a true heart that Jesus is the Son of God has God living in them, and they live in God. This confession is not just repeating words, but trusting Jesus as Lord and following Him in daily life. Real faith joins the believer in a close bond with God.

Believers have come to understand and rely on the love God has for them. Because God is love, the person who continues in love remains in fellowship with God, and God remains in them. Living in love keeps a Christian walking closely with their Creator.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Early church teachers such as Augustine emphasized that by abiding in love, a person makes God their dwelling place and becomes a home for God Himself.

notes.meaning: As believers live in God, love grows mature and complete among them. This gives them peace and confidence as they think about the coming day of judgment, because in this world they reflect the character of Christ. Knowing they are loved by God takes away the dread of facing Him.

differ.view: Boldness at the judgment rests entirely on God's free grace in Christ, with our love serving only as secondary proof that we are His children.
Confidence on judgment day comes because God's love fills the soul, removing inner sin and making the believer holy in this world.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching views love and good works as a real basis for meeting God without terror at the judgment.

notes.meaning: There is no terror in genuine love, because mature love drives out painful fear. Dread of God comes from a guilty conscience that expects punishment. A person who lives in that kind of torment has not yet fully grown in understanding God's perfect love.

differ.view: Love casts out slavish fear of punishment and human threats, but a healthy, reverent fear of God as Father remains in the Christian life.
Believers grow through distinct stages, moving from fear without love, to mixed fear and love, until mature love removes all tormenting fear.
Tormenting fear is rooted in inner sin, which is entirely cleansed away when a believer receives the blessing of perfect love.
The love that casts out fear is primarily God's love for us, which faith grasps to bring quiet peace to a troubled conscience.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Ancient teachers like Augustine taught that fear enters first like a needle to pull the thread of love into the soul, fading away as love grows.

notes.meaning: Christians are able to love because God loved them first. He did not wait for humans to turn to Him, but took the first step while we were still sinners. His prior love gives us both the reason and the power to love Him and our neighbors.

If someone claims to love God while holding hatred against a brother or sister in Christ, that person is telling a lie. It is impossible to love the invisible God whom we have not seen if we cannot love the real people right in front of our eyes. Caring for others is the test of whether our love for God is real.

God gave a clear rule that whoever loves Him must also love their fellow believers. Loving God and loving other people are bound together in one single command. We obey the Lord only when we show genuine care to His children.
